question.text: What does 'open interest' in the currency futures market represent?

answer.text: The total number of outstanding (unsettled) contracts for an underlying asset
The total trading volume for the day
The number of new contracts opened during the day
The difference between buy and sell orders

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 52 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) defines open interest as the total number of contracts outstanding (not yet settled) for an underlying asset. Because every long position is matched by a corresponding short position, only one side is counted, and open interest indicates the depth of the market. The Trap: Open interest is not the same as trading volume (which counts all trades on a given day), not just the number of new contracts opened intraday, and not the order imbalance between buys and sells. Note: Interpretations linking rising/falling open interest to new money, bullish sentiment, or unwinding are not stated on page 52 and are not used here.
